corpus.snapshot_preparation: Validated SQLite backup captured after the benchmark; removed only IDs absent from the original 10000-record corpus. All retained durable fields were independently verified identical to their source rows. Working database remains unchanged.

evaluation.method: Hand-authored, predeclared queries identify designated relevant synthetic fixture facts by natural content. Hit@k tests whether any labelled target appears by rank k. MRR@5 is 1/rank of the first target, or zero when absent in five results.
limits: Synthetic authored cases are diagnostics, not a representative sample of human queries or real-world accuracy.
Several queries reuse each fact; query observations are correlated. No confidence interval is reported.
Labels identify specific target facts, not every potentially relevant background item; no precision, recall, or nDCG is claimed.
Literal, prefix, malformed, contextual, and paraphrase cases are reported separately; the aggregate depends on this deliberately selected query mix.
FTS5 performs lexical matching. Synonyms and zero lexical overlap are not semantic retrieval.
Rows with equal ranking scores use random UUID order, so tied ranks may change when the corpus is regenerated.
Metadata invariants inspect returned samples, with explicit lifecycle/context checks; they do not exhaust every possible query.
evaluation.surface_overlap_method: Accent-folded, casefolded Unicode word tokens compared with target content/category/project; this is a diagnostic approximation, not SQLite's tokenizer.
evaluation.label_notes: 80 queries were authored from the unqueried fixture plan and frozen before the first relevance evaluation. Facts are synthetic and repeat eight topic templates across six project contexts. Queries were manually composed using the disclosed facts, not sampled from real users or independently judged by humans. Several queries reuse facts; this is a deliberately diagnostic query mix. Exact-keyword cases use natural details such as lockfiles, hourly, and keyring rather than artificial fixture markers. Paraphrase questions intentionally test a lexical engine's limitation. Only designated factual targets are labelled; broad ambiguous queries are excluded from hit/MRR averages.

broad_queries.notes: Many corpus records are plausibly relevant; no arbitrary single target is labelled.
Repeated technical topic has many plausible matches; no target-ranking claim.
Multiple preferences and background reports can be relevant.
